review_note: STATUS BOARD — review weekly until Aug 4, 2026, then monthly. Every field must match the official engagement pages before publishing an update.

areas.name: The Meziadin
areas.official: Meziadin River Watershed Salmon Habitat Conservation Planning
areas.partners: Gitanyow Hereditary Chiefs · Nisg̱a'a Lisims Government · Province of BC
areas.mechanism: Proposed ~47,000 ha westward expansion of the Hanna-Tintina Conservancy (24,260 ha, est. 2013)
areas.status: Public comment open — closes Aug 4, 2026, 4 pm PT
areas.next: Engagement continues into fall 2026; final recommendation goes to cabinet
areas.facts: 3% of the Nass watershed by area, roughly 75% of its sockeye. 33 mineral tenures (~12,343 ha) would be retired; ~89% of the Nass South planning area stays open to exploration.

areas.name: The Klappan · Sacred Headwaters
areas.official: Klappan Plan implementation — Zone A + former coal-licence area
areas.territory: Tahltan territory · where the Skeena, Nass and Stikine rise
areas.partners: Tahltan Central Government · Province of BC (Klappan Management Board)
areas.mechanism: Proposed 302,980 ha Park Act conservancy: Zone A (286,580 ha) plus the former Fortune Minerals coal-licence area (16,400 ha)
areas.status: Public comment open — closes Aug 4, 2026, 4 pm PT
areas.next: Final decision by the BC and Tahltan governments after the comment window
areas.facts: Built on the 2019 BC–Tahltan Klappan Plan and the Tahltan Stewardship Plan 'Keep Our Trails Open'. Hunting, fishing, snowmobiling, guide-outfitting and trapping stay in; industrial mining, logging, oil and gas are out.

areas.name: Dene K'éh Kusān
areas.territory: Kaska Dena territory · Liard headwaters and the Kechika
areas.partners: Kaska First Nations · Province of BC
areas.mechanism: Proposed 3,065,128 ha conservancy within the 9.9-million-ha Kaska–BC planning area
areas.status: Public comment open — closes Aug 4, 2026, 4 pm PT
areas.next: Further engagement follows the comment window before cabinet decisions
areas.facts: 'Always Will Be There' in the Kaska language. More than 92% already sits inside the Muskwa-Kechika Management Area; the Dease-Liard plan outside it would be updated to enable exploration in targeted areas. Guide-outfitting and trapping are grandfathered.
